findings.summary: Formula guard misses spill-ghost and pivot cells: toggleCheckboxAt still reports `true` while setData silently no-ops
findings.evidence: The new guard at sheet.ts:3842 only bails on `cell?.f`. Two other cells are equally formula/definition-driven and are silently rejected downstream: (a) a spill ghost cell (`existing?.spillAnchor`) — `setData` returns at sheet.ts:1004 before writing; (b) any cell on a pivot sheet — `setData` returns at sheet.ts:995. In both cases `toggleCheckboxAt` runs `await this.setData(ref, next)` and then `return true`, so callers (view/spreadsheet.ts:366 re-renders, worksheet.ts:4853 re-renders) are told a toggle happened when nothing changed. The same read-only rationale the guard cites ("the formula drives the state") applies to a spill ghost, whose value comes from the anchor formula.

findings.summary: Case-insensitive matching is gated on `checkedValue`/`uncheckedValue` being strictly `undefined`, so a rule that stores the defaults explicitly loses the fix
findings.evidence: `if (rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined)` (data-validation.ts:163). A rule that round-trips through an importer/serializer with the canonical defaults written out explicitly (`checkedValue: 'TRUE'`, `uncheckedValue: 'FALSE'`) is semantically a default boolean checkbox but takes the exact-match branch, so exactly the lowercase `'true'` values the doc-comment says arrive from xlsx/REST/paste render unchecked. Also, an empty-string custom value (`checkedValue: ''`) falls into the exact-match branch and `checkedValueOf` returns `''` (`??` does not fall back for `''`), so a cell holding `''` would be reported checked. No importer sets these fields today, hence low confidence.
searchedFor: grep dataValidations in backend/core/cli for importers

findings.summary: Case-fold fallback does not trim, so externally-pasted values like ` true` still render unchecked
findings.evidence: `return value.toUpperCase() === CHECKBOX_TRUE;` compares untrimmed. The stated motivation is values that "bypass setData normalization" (external paste / REST / xlsx); such values commonly carry surrounding whitespace, which the new branch still rejects, unlike `isValidListValue` (data-validation.ts:202/210) which trims both sides for exactly this reason.
searchedFor: read isValidListValue trimming convention in same file

findings.summary: Formula-guard test asserts only that `f` survives; it never asserts the cell's value was not overwritten, despite the comment claiming "writes no literal"
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/test/sheet/data-validation.test.ts:66-69 comments "Toggle is a no-op: reports false, keeps the formula, writes no literal" but the only post-toggle assertions are `toggleCheckboxAt(...) === false` and `cell?.f === '=1=1'`. `cell?.v` (the formula-computed value the checkbox actually renders from — gridcanvas.ts:1042 uses `cell?.v`) is never asserted before or after, so a regression that preserved `f` while clobbering `v` (or one where the formula never evaluated at all) passes. The test also never verifies the stated rationale that "the formula drives the state" (i.e. that `isCheckboxChecked(rule, cell.v)` is true for `=1=1`).

findings.summary: No test covers the branch where only a custom `checkedValue` is set (uncheckedValue undefined)
findings.evidence: The new guard is `rule.checkedValue === undefined && rule.uncheckedValue === undefined`. The added tests cover (a) both undefined (data-validation.test.ts:93), (b) both set (:107), (c) uncheckedValue-only (:118). The checkedValue-only case — e.g. `{checkedValue: 'true'}` with default `uncheckedValue: 'FALSE'` — is never exercised, so flipping the `&&` to check only `uncheckedValue` (or dropping the `checkedValue === undefined` conjunct) would not fail any test.

findings.summary: The motivating render path (lowercase 'true' rendering as checked) has no test at the renderer/view level
findings.evidence: The stated motivation for case-folding is that imported/pasted lowercase values "must still render checked"; the only consumer is `isCheckboxChecked(rule, cell?.v)` at packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042. Coverage stops at the pure helper — no view/gridcanvas or browser-visual test asserts a cell containing 'true' under a checkbox rule renders in the checked state. Grep for isCheckboxChecked found only data-validation.test.ts and gridcanvas.ts as call sites; no gridcanvas checkbox test file surfaced.

findings.summary: toggle from a lowercase unchecked value ('false' → TRUE) is untested
findings.evidence: The new test asserts `toggleCheckboxValue(rule, 'true') === CHECKBOX_FALSE` but not the symmetric `toggleCheckboxValue(rule, 'false') === CHECKBOX_TRUE`, which is the case where the `toUpperCase` fallback must return false rather than throw off the toggle direction.

findings.summary: Case-insensitive TRUE/FALSE recognition is re-implemented locally instead of reusing the existing shared boolean recognition in `inferInput` (`input.ts:241-247`), which the issue itself cites as the precedent. A tiny shared helper (e.g. `isBooleanLiteral`/`parseBooleanLiteral`) exported from `input.ts` would keep the two case-folding rules in lockstep; the inline version can drift if input parsing ever accepts more boolean spellings. The no-allocation argument is real but could live inside such a helper. Preference, not a blocker.
findings.evidence: data-validation.ts:163-167 does `value.toUpperCase() === CHECKBOX_TRUE` while input.ts:241-247 already lower-cases and compares to 'true'/'false'.

findings.summary: `toggleCheckboxAt` now returns `false` for two semantically different outcomes: "no checkbox rule here" and "there is a checkbox rule but it is formula-backed and read-only". Callers (worksheet.ts:3405 click, worksheet.ts:4853 Space) only use the boolean to decide whether to re-render, so nothing breaks today, but neither path can surface "this checkbox is driven by a formula" feedback (GS shows the control as non-interactive). Worth noting in the design doc or a follow-up if any UX affordance is wanted.

findings.summary: Unbounded `value.toUpperCase()` on the per-repaint render path over attacker/collaborator-controlled cell text
findings.evidence: `isCheckboxChecked` is called once per visible checkbox per repaint from `gridcanvas.ts:1042` with the raw cell value (`cell?.v`). The new fallback at data-validation.ts:166 short-circuits only on the exact strings `TRUE`/`FALSE`; every other value now allocates a full uppercased copy of the string on each frame. Cell values are not length-bounded anywhere I could find in packages/sheets (no MaxCell/maxLength constant), and they can be supplied by a remote collaborator (Yorkie doc), an xlsx import, or a paste — the very sources this change cites as motivation. A peer who writes a multi-megabyte string into a cell covered by a checkbox rule causes a per-frame O(n) allocation + case-map in the other participants' render loop (jank / memory churn), where the pre-change code did a length-short-circuited `===`. Impact is client-side resource consumption only, not data exposure; I did not build a PoC, hence low confidence. A length guard (e.g. skip the fallback when `value.length > CHECKBOX_TRUE.length`) removes the vector entirely, since no value longer than 5 chars can uppercase to `TRUE`.

findings.summary: Formula read-only guard is a parity/UX guard, not an enforced write boundary — other write paths still overwrite a formula-backed checkbox cell
findings.evidence: `toggleCheckboxAt` now returns false when `cell?.f` is set, but this is not an access-control boundary: `Sheet.setData` (and paste/fill/removeData) remain reachable for the same ref with no equivalent check, so the cell's formula is still overwritable by ordinary edits. I enumerated every caller of `toggleCheckboxAt` (view/spreadsheet.ts:363, view/worksheet.ts:3405 click path, view/worksheet.ts:4853 Space path) and each is already gated on `this.readOnly`/`this._readOnly` before reaching the model, so the change neither adds nor weakens a permission gate. Flagging only so the guard is not later read as an authorization control; no bypass of an existing security gate found.
searchedFor: Grep checkbox|CHECKBOX in packages/backend (no server-side path)

findings.summary: View layer left inconsistent with the new read-only rule: the renderer still draws a normal interactive checkbox glyph for a formula-backed cell (gridcanvas.ts:1042 / renderCellCheckbox), and the click hit-test still accepts the glyph rect and calls `toggleCheckboxAt` (worksheet.ts:3394-3406), unconditionally selecting, `finishEditing()`-ing and re-rendering even though the toggle is now always a no-op. Users get a clickable-looking control with no feedback; no consumer was updated to reflect the new read-only state (e.g. dimmed glyph or skipped hit-test).
findings.evidence: packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:3405 ignores the (now sometimes-false) return and calls `this.render()`; packages/sheets/src/view/gridcanvas.ts:1042 renders the glyph identically regardless of `cell?.f`.

@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
+# Checkbox data-validation bug fixes
+
+Follow-ups from the data-validation design doc (`docs/design/sheets/data-validation.md`,
+Phase-1 "Not yet guarded" note). Two clear correctness bugs in the shipped
+checkbox control, each self-contained.
+
+## Bugs
+
+1. **Formula cell is not read-only under a checkbox rule.**
+   `Sheet.toggleCheckboxAt` (`sheet.ts:3834`) reads `cell?.v` and writes a
+   literal `TRUE`/`FALSE` via `setData` without checking `cell.f`. Toggling a
+   checkbox that sits over a formula cell **overwrites the formula**. Design
+   intent: a formula-backed checkbox is read-only (the formula drives the
+   state) — Google Sheets / Excel parity. Both the click path
+   (`worksheet.ts:3405`) and the Space path (`worksheet.ts:4853`) route through
+   `toggleCheckboxAt`, so one guard fixes both.
+
+2. **`isCheckboxChecked` is case-sensitive.**
+   `isCheckboxChecked` (`data-validation.ts:149`) compares `value === 'TRUE'`
+   exactly, so a cell holding `"true"` renders **unchecked**. `setData`
+   normalizes typed input to `"TRUE"`, but values arriving via xlsx import /
+   REST API / external paste can be lowercase and bypass normalization. The
+   formula engine (`formula.ts:1054`) and input parser (`input.ts:242`) already
+   treat `TRUE`/`FALSE` case-insensitively; the render/toggle path should match.
+   Fix scope: **default boolean checkbox only** (no custom `checkedValue`) —
+   a custom checked value stays an exact string match (GS parity).
+
+## Plan (TDD)
+
+- [x] Model test: `isCheckboxChecked` matches `"true"`/`"True"`/`"TRUE"` for a
+      default rule; a custom-value rule stays exact-match.
+- [x] Model fix: `isCheckboxChecked` case-insensitive for the fully-default
+      boolean checkbox only; `toggleCheckboxValue` inherits the fix (delegates).
+- [x] Sheet test: `toggleCheckboxAt` over a formula cell is a no-op — returns
+      `false`, leaves `cell.f` intact, writes no `v`.
+- [x] Sheet fix: guard `toggleCheckboxAt` on `cell?.f`.
+- [x] `pnpm test` (sheets) green; `pnpm verify:fast` green (EXIT 0).
+- [x] Update design doc Phase-1 "Not yet guarded" note (both now fixed).
+
+## Review
+
+High-effort workflow code review (`Workflow code-review`, 4 finders + verify)
+surfaced two findings, both addressed:
+
+- **[0] correctness (PLAUSIBLE)** — case-fold branch was gated only on
+  `checkedValue === undefined`, so a rule with a custom `uncheckedValue` that
+  upper-cases to `"TRUE"` inverted state. Fixed: case-folding now requires
+  *both* custom values absent; added a regression test.
+- **[1] cleanup (CONFIRMED)** — `value.toUpperCase()` allocated per repaint,
+  against the file's no-alloc convention. Fixed: canonical `TRUE`/`FALSE`
+  short-circuit before the `toUpperCase` fallback.
+
+A refuted finding ("silently depends on `CHECKBOX_TRUE` being uppercase") was
+dismissed by the verifier — `CHECKBOX_TRUE` is a module constant.
+
+Both bugs are model/Sheet-level; the click and Space view paths route through
+`toggleCheckboxAt` and the render path through `isCheckboxChecked`, so no
+view-layer change was needed. View-layer smoke deferred (Phase-1 precedent).
+
+## Out of scope (separate follow-ups)
+
+- Space range-uniform "set all checked" (parity feature, not a bug).
+- Merged-cell glyph/hit-test mismatch.
+- Eager `FALSE` materialization for `COUNTIF`.
+- Custom checkbox values UI.
+
+## Review
+
+(filled after implementation)

samples.summary: Unbounded `value.toUpperCase()` on the per-repaint render path over attacker/collaborator-controlled cell text
samples.evidence: `isCheckboxChecked` is called once per visible checkbox per repaint from `gridcanvas.ts:1042` with the raw cell value (`cell?.v`). The new fallback at data-validation.ts:166 short-circuits only on the exact strings `TRUE`/`FALSE`; every other value now allocates a full uppercased copy of the string on each frame. Cell values are not length-bounded anywhere I could find in packages/sheets (no MaxCell/maxLength constant), and they can be supplied by a remote collaborator (Yorkie doc), an xlsx import, or a paste — the very sources this change cites as motivation. A peer who writes a multi-megabyte string into a cell covered by a checkbox rule causes a per-frame O(n) allocation + case-map in the other participants' render loop (jank / memory churn), where the pre-change code did a length-short-circuited `===`. Impact is client-side resource consumption only, not data exposure; I did not build a PoC, hence low confidence. A length guard (e.g. skip the fallback when `value.length > CHECKBOX_TRUE.length`) removes the vector entirely, since no value longer than 5 chars can uppercase to `TRUE`.

samples.summary: Formula read-only guard is a parity/UX guard, not an enforced write boundary — other write paths still overwrite a formula-backed checkbox cell
samples.evidence: `toggleCheckboxAt` now returns false when `cell?.f` is set, but this is not an access-control boundary: `Sheet.setData` (and paste/fill/removeData) remain reachable for the same ref with no equivalent check, so the cell's formula is still overwritable by ordinary edits. I enumerated every caller of `toggleCheckboxAt` (view/spreadsheet.ts:363, view/worksheet.ts:3405 click path, view/worksheet.ts:4853 Space path) and each is already gated on `this.readOnly`/`this._readOnly` before reaching the model, so the change neither adds nor weakens a permission gate. Flagging only so the guard is not later read as an authorization control; no bypass of an existing security gate found.
searchedFor: Grep checkbox|CHECKBOX in packages/backend (no server-side path)

samples.summary: New formula read-only guard is bypassed for spilled (ghost) cells: `toggleCheckboxAt` checks only `cell?.f`, but a cell produced by an array-formula spill carries `spillAnchor` (no `f`). The guard passes, `toggleCheckboxValue` computes a value, and `setData` then silently returns at sheet.ts:1004 (`if (existing?.spillAnchor) return;`). Net effect: the checkbox under a formula-driven spill range still reports `true` ("a toggle happened") to the click/Space callers, which re-render as if the state changed, while nothing was written — exactly the read-only-formula case the guard was added for, minus the correct `false` return. Fix belongs on the new guard in sheet.ts (also bail on `cell?.spillAnchor`).

verdict.reason: The mechanism is real as quoted (toggleCheckboxAt at sheet.ts:3834-3848 guards only cell?.f; ghost cells written at calculator.ts:128 as {v, spillAnchor} have no f; getCell at sheet.ts:872 returns them unchanged), but the protected mutation is already guarded downstream: setData returns at sheet.ts:1004 before any store.set/delete, before dependency expansion and before calculate(), and the batch opened at sheet.ts:998 is closed by the finally at sheet.ts:1064-1066. So nothing is written, no formula or spill is overwritten, no invariant is violated and no batch leaks — the read-only semantics hold. The only residual effect of the incorrect `true` is a redundant repaint of the unchanged, formula-driven value: spreadsheet.ts:366 and worksheet.ts:4854 merely call render(), and worksheet.ts:3405 ignores the return value and renders unconditionally anyway. A repo-wide grep shows those are the only consumers of the boolean; none persists, broadcasts, or records undo based on it. That places the real residual in the rubric's `minor` band (a consumer that still works but is now inconsistent), not major/critical — no data loss, crash, or defeated guard on a reachable path — so it is not merge-gating, even though also bailing on cell?.spillAnchor would be a reasonable cleanup.
